content.mission: Maintain law and order, preserve public peace, prevent and detect crimes and apprehend offenders, as the Police Force Act 2004 sets out, using force only as the law allows.

sequence.label: Prevent the offence
sequence.action: Intervene to prevent an offence you have reasonable grounds to suspect may be committed, using all lawful means, including removing a person from a place.

sequence.label: Barriers
sequence.action: Place barriers across roads or public places where needed to maintain order or prevent crime, and stop vehicles at them.

sequence.label: Order in public places
sequence.action: Preserve order in public places and regulate traffic, removing obstructions.

sequence.label: Special powers
sequence.action: Where the Minister has made an activation order and the Commissioner a special authorisation, exercise the special powers in the target area: cordons, road closures, movement control and searches.

sequence.label: Arrest
sequence.action: Arrest by touching or confining the person unless they submit; if they forcibly resist, use all reasonable means necessary.

sequence.label: Receive detainees
sequence.action: Take over any person arrested or detained by SAF servicemen deployed in aid of the civil authorities.

never.action: Restrain an arrested person more than is necessary to prevent escape
Use special powers outside a target area or without a special authorisation in effect
never.why: POSSPA 2018 Part 4 powers are exercised pursuant to a special authorisation, in its target area.

hand_offs.when: A suspected explosive device or explosive ordnance is found.
An incident involves armed criminals or hostages and needs a tactical armed response.
The consequences of a major disaster or civil emergency need managing.

legal_authorities.power: Functions of the Police Force: maintain law and order, preserve public peace, prevent and detect crimes and apprehend offenders; duties include regulating traffic and preserving order in public places.
Any police officer may erect barriers across a public road or place to maintain order or prevent or detect crime, and take reasonable steps to stop vehicles and people passing them.
A police officer may command an unlawful assembly, or an assembly of five or more likely to disturb the peace, to disperse, and may disperse it by force if it does not.

An officer must use all lawful means to prevent a suspected offence, and may do what is likely to cause death or grievous hurt when necessary to apprehend a person doing or about to do a terrorist act.
If a person forcibly resists or evades arrest, all reasonable means necessary may be used; an arrested person must not be restrained more than is necessary to prevent escape.

legal_authorities.instrument: Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Act 2018
legal_authorities.power: Under a Ministerial activation order and a special authorisation, police may cordon, close roads, control movement and search in the target area, using reasonably necessary force, including lethal weapons, to enforce them.

An authorised officer may remove or arrest, with reasonable force, a person in a protected area or place without good reason; force may extend to causing death if the person does not stop after three directions.
A person arrested or detained by a serviceman deployed in aid of civil authorities must be handed to a police officer as soon as practicable.

conditions.when: Command an unlawful assembly, or one of five or more likely to disturb the peace, to disperse.
Touch or confine a person to arrest them; use all reasonable means necessary if they forcibly resist or try to evade arrest.
The officer has reasonable grounds to believe a person is doing or about to do something that may amount to a terrorist act, and the act is necessary to apprehend them.
Under a special authorisation in force, to stop people or vehicles entering a cordoned area or to enforce road-closure and movement orders, as reasonably necessary.

principles: Force must be reasonably necessary (CPC s. 75(2); POSSPA ss. 18 to 20).
An arrested person must not be restrained more than is necessary to prevent escape (CPC s. 76).
Officers evaluate the threat and decide the force needed in real time (MHA, 26 Feb 2021).
Complaints of disproportionate force are investigated by MHA (MHA, 26 Feb 2021).
use_of_force.command_authority: The officer's own reasonable belief under CPC s. 63(2); POSSPA powers need the Minister's activation order and the Commissioner's special authorisation.
